problem.label: A. Research Problem
problem.text: Low-code platforms accelerate delivery but often produce systems that are tightly coupled, opaque, and difficult to extend beyond their original boundaries. The problem is not speed — it is the lack of architectural clarity underneath.

question.label: B. Research Question
question.text: How can a headless low-code web application builder be architected so that its abstraction layers remain composable, replaceable, and decoupled from any specific presentation surface?

direction.label: C. Research Direction
direction.text: The direction treats the builder as a set of independent layers — modelling, schema, runtime, and rendering — each with explicit contracts. The goal is not to build another platform, but to describe an architecture that other builders could adopt.

current.label: D. Current
current.outcome: No results yet. This section will be updated as the research progresses.
